Share files anywhere.
Leave no trace.

DeepDarkShare sends photos, videos and any file straight from one phone to another through the Tor network. No account. No phone number. No server in the middle.

  • End-to-end encrypted
  • One-time hidden addresses
  • Zero data collected
  • Works across networks & countries

How it works

Three taps, two phones, one hidden route

The receiver's phone creates a brand-new hidden address on the Tor network. The sender reaches it through six encrypted relays. The address disappears as soon as the receiver is done.

1

Tap Receive

A one-time QR code appears. Can't scan? Show the code and read or send it instead.

2

Pick files and Send

Choose photos, videos or anything from Files, then scan the QR code or type the code.

3

Accept and done

The receiver sees who is sending what, taps Accept, and the files arrive, checked and intact.

Built on Tor

Your files never touch a server

Every transfer runs phone-to-phone through Tor onion services, the same technology journalists and activists rely on. Your IP address and location stay hidden from the other side and from everyone in between.

  • A fresh hidden address every time. Each receive code is a new .onion address that only exists while the Receive screen is open.
  • Two layers of encryption. Tor's own, plus ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a key that exists only in the code.
  • Every file verified. Sizes and SHA-256 checksums are checked before a file is saved.
  • A live onion map. Watch the relays your transfer travels through, country by country.

The right person, every time

Nothing arrives without your yes

Files can only reach the phone that showed the code: only that phone holds its hidden address's key. And nothing is saved until the receiver agrees.

  • Accept or decline. See the sender's name and every file with its size before anything is written.
  • Safety code. Four emoji on both screens. If they match, you're connected to the phone you meant.
  • Wrong code? Turned away. A sender without the right key is dropped before you're even asked.
  • One at a time. While a transfer runs, anyone else is politely told you're busy.

Everything you need

Made for real-life sharing

The simplicity of a nearby-share app, without the nearby part.

Any file, any size

Photos and videos in their original quality, documents, music, archives: up to 500 files at once.

No setup to grant

No location, Wi-Fi hotspot, Bluetooth or contacts. Photos come through Apple's private picker, so the app only sees what you choose.

Scan, paste or type

QR code in person, a link over any messenger, or a short typed code with built-in typo detection.

History you control

Every transfer is listed on your phone only. Received files also appear in the Files app. Delete anything, anytime.

Anonymous by default

You get a random name like "Violet Fox 27". Change it or keep it: nobody learns your number or account.

Dark, or light

A calm dark-grey and violet design, with an optional light theme you choose in the app.

A closer look

Every screen, focused on one job

What it doesn't do

Privacy by leaving things out

  • No accounts. Nothing to sign up for, nothing to log in to.
  • No servers. There is no DeepDarkShare server to store, scan or leak your files.
  • No tracking or analytics. No ads, no trackers, no usage data.
  • No public content. No feeds or directories: just one-to-one transfers you agree to.
  • No location. The map shows your region from your phone's settings, never your position.
  • No leftovers. Hidden addresses are thrown away; interrupted transfers are cleaned up.

Questions

Good to know

Do both people need to be on the same Wi-Fi?

No. Transfers go over the internet through Tor, so the sender and receiver can be on different networks, mobile data, or in different countries.

How fast is it?

Tor adds privacy, not speed. Once connected, typical transfers run at a few hundred kilobytes per second; the first connection after opening the app takes a little longer while Tor starts.

Can someone intercept my files?

Files travel end-to-end encrypted to a hidden address that only the receiver's phone controls. Relays in between can't read them. For extra certainty, compare the four-emoji safety code on both screens.

What happens to the receive code afterwards?

It stops working the moment the receiver leaves the Receive screen. Every new receive creates a brand-new code.

Does it work on iPad?

Yes. DeepDarkShare runs on iPhone and iPad with iOS 16 or later.
